_yearHistory: THREE INDEPENDENT items, all on the physical CD, all pointing to 2003:
1. Booklet, orchestra biography: 'Philharmonisches Orchester Lugansk wurde im
Sommer 1945 gegruendet ... Im Laufe von 58 Jahren hat das Orchester ...'
1945 + 58 = 2003. The strongest single item.
2. Booklet, Kurt Schmid biography: a dated list whose last entry is 2002, so the
booklet was written in 2002 or 2003.
3. Highest opus printed on the back inlay is Schmid's 'Auf nach Lugansk',
Op. 327, catalogued 2003 in the Johann Strauss Society work list
(https://johann-strauss.org.uk/composers-n-z.php?id=264). The disc's other
Schmid opus numbers are Op. 313 (2001) and Op. 324 (between 2002 and 2003).
Consistent but NOT independent: track 8 honours Michael Miess, Austrian
ambassador in Kyiv 2001-2006, which only bounds the window.
*** CORRECTION, 2026-08-24. An earlier version of this entry claimed the disc
face marking '03/2' was DECISIVE proof of 2003, on the stated basis that Egermann
Produktion used year/sequence catalogue numbers. THAT CLAIM WAS UNSUPPORTED and
has been withdrawn. The label has no other documented releases to compare against
(its MusicBrainz label entity 18f8ef7e-3b2d-4e8e-b24d-48321f68d3f6 has zero
releases attached; no Egermann catalogue number is findable online). It was also
CIRCULAR: the year was inferred from the booklet first, and then used to interpret
'03/2', which was then presented as independent confirmation — the same evidence
counted twice. '03/2' is recorded below as an observation only.
OBSERVED, interpretation withheld: the disc face is printed '03/2' below the
Compact Disc Digital Audio logo, where a catalogue number normally sits. It is
consistent with 2003; it is not evidence for it.
EVIDENCE POINTING EARLIER, and why it is discounted: the back inlay prints a
Vienna phone number with the pre-1998 area code '0222'. That dates the label's
design template, not the disc, and is contradicted by all three items above.
NO DATE IN THE PRESSING: matrix 'A0100459099-0101' identifies Sony DADC Austria
(Anif) as the plant; it is a sequential job number carrying no readable date.
RESIDUAL AMBIGUITY: 'im Laufe von 58 Jahren' read as SEASONS (1945/46 as the
first) gives the 2002/03 season and a January 2003 concert; read as completed
calendar years it is only reached in summer 2003, which would point at January
2004. 2003 is the better reading and matches Op. 327's catalogue year.

*** NEEDS A DECISION BEFORE THE MIDDLE BAND SHIPS — raised 2026-08-24 ***
'Philharmonia Orchestra London, Georg Randolph Warren (1982)' appears to come
from the ALFRED SCHOLZ budget-reissue world. Evidence, all from MusicBrainz's own
cataloguing:
- the ensemble entity 67da2cc7 is disambiguated 'Alfred Scholz related, not the
London Philharmonic, the Philharmonia or the New Philharmonia';
- sibling entities are flagged the same way: 'American Philharmonia Orchestra'
('Alfred Scholz related') and 'New Philharmonia Orchestra of London'
('bogus name used on budget releases');
- the conductor entity d2f3f838 'George Randolph Warren' is typed Person but
carries no life span, no country and no begin-area — just 'conductor'.
Scholz-era budget labels routinely issued recordings under INVENTED orchestra and
conductor names, and re-badged existing performances. So this recording's
attributed ensemble and conductor may not correspond to real entities at all.
WHY THIS MATTERS HERE, and it is not a data-tidiness point:
1. The middle band displays conductor + year. We would be naming a conductor
who may never have existed, with museum authority behind it.
2. Plan section 5.5 calls for GEN-AI PORTRAITS of each conductor, labelled as
AI impressions of real, named people. Generating a portrait of a probable
pseudonym is a different and worse proposition.
3. The exhibit's premise is comparing INTERPRETATIONS. If this is a re-badged
copy of another ensemble's performance, it is not an independent
interpretation, and the comparison it appears to offer is illusory.
OPTIONS, none of them free — the curated 8 were chosen in plan section 5.2 for
annotation coverage and contrast, so dropping one has a real cost:
a. Keep it, display the ensemble name only, and no conductor or portrait.
b. Keep it and label it honestly as a budget reissue of uncertain attribution.
c. Replace it in the curated set. Recheck the 4 VPO / 4 non-VPO balance and the
annotation coverage figures if so.
d. Investigate first: Scholz reissues are often traceable to the original
performance, which would let the recording stay with correct attribution.
This is an editorial and factual call for the project, not a development one.
DECISION 2026-08-25: option d — investigated. FINDINGS (research session 17):
CONFIRMED — the source release: track 7 (8:15) of 'Beruehmte Ouvertueren',
Saphir (Intercord budget imprint) INT 830.814, P-1982 Intercord, credited
'Philharmonia Orchestra (London), George Randolph Warren'; LP INT 130.814
(1985), cassette INT 430.814, and 3-CD box INT 885.929 (1992). The exhibit's
'1982' is the Intercord P-date, not a documented session date. MB releases
Discogs release 11909240, master 1438895.
CONFIRMED — the audio is the standard Scholz-catalogue Fledermaus: AcoustID
b9290546-ea31-447b-b200-fa684b7757ce (19 fingerprints, ~800 submissions) ties
it to the same audio sold as 'Orchester der Wiener Volksoper / London Festival
Orchestra / Igor Gogol / Alfred Scholz' (the Pilz family, release-credited
'New Philharmonia Orchestra London, Alfred Scholz'), 'London Symphony
Orchestra, Alfred Scholz' (MB: 'pseudonym, not the real LSO'), and 'Royal
Promenade Orchestra, Alfred Gehardt' — the latter two names ARE on the
canonical MB Scholz fake-artist lists. Acoustic identification, not inference.
STRONG — 'George Randolph Warren' is a fictitious Intercord/Scholz house name,
in use 1973-1996, always with paper orchestras; the same tape pool appears as
'Ralph Dixon, Philharmonia Orchestra' (Sonocord 1984) at identical timings.
Caveat, honestly: Warren is NOT on the canonical MB Scholz pseudonym list
(list is explicitly incomplete; transcribed and checked — no Warren, no Dixon,
no Gogol).
NOT IDENTIFIED — the real performers. No source names the actual orchestra or
conductor; candidates from the Scholz literature (Vienna Volksoper Orchestra,
'Suedeutsche Philharmonie' pool, ORF/SWF radio tapes) are plausible, none
evidenced for this track. NOTE: the interpretation itself is real and distinct
— no evidence it duplicates any other recording in the corpus — so the
comparison the exhibit offers stands; only the NAMING is fake.
What would settle more: fingerprint our own file against AcoustID b9290546
(closes the loop cheaply); audio comparison against Volksoper-era commercial
recordings; Intercord production ledgers (catalogue passed via EMI).
REMAINING CHOICE (a or b shapes, c is now pointless since the performance is
genuinely distinct): how the middle band and strip caption should read.
